questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Rational Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=\frac{3-x}{{x}^{2}-3x}$ is continuous.
questions.worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3-x}{{x}^{2}-3x} \\  & =\frac{3-x}{x(x-3)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{x},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $x\ne 3.$

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded points $x=0$ and $x=3.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,0),$ $(0,3),$ and $(3,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,0)\cup (0,3)\cup (3,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on this union of intervals.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Rational Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=\frac{x-2}{4{x}^{2}-16x+16}$ is continuous.
questions.worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x-2}{4{x}^{2}-16x+16} \\  & =\frac{x-2}{4({x}^{2}-4x+4)} \\  & =\frac{x-2}{4(x-2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4(x-2)}\end{aligned}
$$

 

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded point $x=2.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,2)$ and $(2,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,2)\cup (2,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on these intervals.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Logarithmic Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Find the largest interval of continuity for the function $f(x)=\operatorname{log}⁡(3-18x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The logarithmic function $\operatorname{log}⁡(3-18x)$ is continuous at all points in its domain. However, the logarithm is only defined for positive inputs, so to find its domain, we set the expression inside the logarithm to be greater than zero:

$$
3-18x>0\,⟹\,18x<3\,⟹\,x<\frac{1}{6}
$$

Therefore, the function $f(x)=\operatorname{log}⁡(3-18x)$ is continuous on the interval $(-\infty ,\frac{1}{6}).$

questions.worked_solution:
Trigonometric functions are continuous at all points in their respective domains.

The function $\operatorname{sin}⁡2x$ is continuous over the entire interval $[\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}],$ but the function $\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is not defined at $x=\pi .$ 

Therefore, the domain of $f(x)$ consists of the union of the intervals $[\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ),$ and $(\pi ,\frac{3\pi }{2}],$ namely
